correctness.rationale: The source defines an irreducible plane pencil, and the first fixed field is independently identified by \(a=x+y\), \(b=xy\). The smoothness of \(D(a,b)=0\) is proved directly from \(D_a=D_b=0\), forcing \(a,b\in\mathbb F_q\) and then \(\lambda=\pm1\), excluded; its unique point at infinity is smooth. The quadratic reconstruction of \(b\) from \(t,w\) proves these generate precisely the second fixed field. Fixed points of inversion are \(q+1\) distinct points on \(b=1\), with no others; Riemann–Hurwitz therefore gives genus \((q-1)^2/4\). In characteristic three exact polynomial reduction, Weierstrass invariants, and the derivative of the j rational map prove the elliptic model, its supersingular member and both ramification partitions. The decoded SymPy checker confirms defining algebraic identities for \(q\in\{3,5,7,9,11,13\}\) and fixed-point squarefreeness in several prime fields; finite samples are not substituted for the parameter-uniform proof. All quotients refer to smooth normalizations.

value.rationale: The invariant-field construction produces an explicit, parameter-uniform intermediate quotient of a natural large-symmetry pencil, with exact genus \(h^2\) for every odd prime power q. The \(q=3\) special case gives a genuine elliptic quotient whose j-map determines the ordinary/supersingular locus, separable degree and wild/tame ramification. These are natural geometric and arithmetic invariants not supplied by the source first-quotient description; the result is neither a mere reparameterization nor an arbitrary small computation.
